question: Students are validating natural convection limits using an adjustable horizontal porous layer bounded by isothermal copper sheets. The cavity contains a porous matrix filled with silicone oil, and the temperature difference is increased until convection loops initiate. In Run A, with a layer height of $H_A = 10~\text{cm}$, the onset of natural convection occurs at $\Delta T_{\text{crit}, A} = 12^\circ\text{C}$. If the setup is kept identical except the height is decreased to $H_B = 5~\text{cm}$ in Run B, what is the new critical temperature difference $\Delta T_{\text{crit}, B}$? Give your answer in $\text{}^\circ\text{C}$ rounded to 1 decimal place.

answers.feedback: Correct! Since $\text{Ra}_m \propto \Delta T_{\text{crit}} H$ is constant for the same porous medium, fluid, and boundaries, halving $H$ doubles $\Delta T_{\text{crit}}$ from $12^\circ\text{C}$ to $24.0^\circ\text{C}$.
Not quite. Halving $\Delta T_{\text{crit}}$ treats it as directly proportional to $H$, whereas in the porous Rayleigh number $\text{Ra}_m$, $\Delta T_{\text{crit}}$ scales inversely with $H$.
Not quite. Changing the layer height $H$ changes the critical temperature difference $\Delta T_{\text{crit}}$ needed to reach the critical Rayleigh number.

Close, but check the scaling exponent on $H$ in the porous Rayleigh number $\text{Ra}_m$—for Darcy flow in a porous layer, $\text{Ra}_m$ is linear in $H$, not quadratic ($H^3$ is for clear-fluid Rayleigh–Bénard convection).

Not quite. Recall the porous medium Rayleigh number $\text{Ra}_m = \frac{g \beta \Delta T K H}{\nu \alpha_{\text{eff}}}$ and how $\Delta T_{\text{crit}}$ depends on $H$ when all other parameters remain fixed. Check the hint or full solution below if needed.
